title: ZOMBRA update, building a zombie survival game with Claude Code and Codex
author: Straight-Tea-8564
selftext:
I shared an early version of ZOMBRA here recently. I have since updated the character art and expanded the world beyond the abandoned city, with a survivor base, ruins and a pickup escort mission. Here is the new trailer.

The game uses JavaScript and Phaser, with help from Claude Code and Codex. Much of the pixel art is drawn procedurally in code. For the trailer, the game's studio runs scripted shots inside the engine, without the HUD.

I gave specific feedback to keep characters moving while firing, alternate fights between the city and ruins, time the cuts to the music and lower the music slightly during narration. Watching the actual footage and correcting individual moments made a big difference.

It is still in development for solo and online co-op play. You can watch the trailer and join the launch waitlist at https://zombra.online/.

comments.author: AkiraVero
comments.body: Looks really cool, thanks for sharing! Do you know when it may be available for testing? I'm developing a similar pixel art RPG style of game as-well where the majority of art is done through code.

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body: Thank you! I may be able to open a public test as early as next week, but that's still tentative. I'm working on the missions and co-op, and I'll share updates at https://zombra.online. It's cool to hear about your RPG too! Do you have any footage or screenshots to share?

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body:
Thanks for your response! I'm looking forward to trying it. I have a website that I haven't been publicly advertising yet with a demo (trying to get a lot of bug fixing done and website fixes first). You can check it out if you want! lumoriagame.com. 

I would love if you could comment on my demo and website as well! The demo is derived from the game with a lot of "demo" only changes and simplifications.I

I also have a really bad trailer that I'm working on that's from in-game rendering and clips made by Claude as the director, but I feel like it has a long way to go. I'm especially having trouble working on the sound and trying to not have like overlapping sounds / background music / clipping when going from one scene to another.

 I feel like it may be because AI is not very good at "hearing" audio I guess, it's difficult for AI. Or I just need to learn to prompt him better. I'm considering investing in something like Gemini listening to the audio to try to help, but it's been a struggle.

  
P.S. I played your other game Pawbound and was really enchanted by it. Is there any plans to continue working on that game? I really enjoyed it.

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body: Thanks for sharing Lumoria! It is cool to hear you are also making art through code. For my trailer, I also had to listen to and adjust the audio manually. Separating voice, music and effects and paying attention to the transitions helped a lot. And yes, I am still developing Pawbound! It is a huge game with many possibilities, so new updates come at a much slower pace. Right now I am working on the familiars system: companions that follow the player throughout their adventure. Really glad you enjoyed it!

comments.author: Lambisexual
comments.body: I've always wondered how the animations are actually made and even looks good? Every time I've tried to dip my toe in making the AI do animations it always looks horrendous. Granted I've been using GPT not Claude for coding, but still.

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body: In ZOMBRA, the characters are assembled from parts such as the head, torso, arms and legs, and their movements are controlled through code. I use Claude Code and Codex to help build and refine those routines, but the results come from a lot of reviewing inside the game. Working on one small action at a time and checking it visually has been essential.
